head: Your GPS
is lying
to you
body: Our app once clocked a parked car at 400 kmph. The phone was completely sure.
Swipe for why, and the fix.

head: Confident.
Cooperative.
*Often wrong.
slides.caption: GPS looks like truth. It behaves like a witness who took a hit to the head, and it has never once suspected itself.

head: Tunnels,
towers,
garages
body: In a tunnel it repeats the last spot for about 40 seconds, then jumps to catch up.
A big jump over a tiny time is your 400 kmph.

items.title: Catch the liars
items.sub: if a reading needs rocket acceleration, drop it

items.title: Dead reckoning
items.sub: estimate from the IMU and last good heading

items.title: Fuse, do not pick
items.sub: weight each signal by how much you trust it now

head: 50% to 95%
body: Trip accuracy, in production, on real drives.
Almost every point we were missing was a moment the phone lied with total confidence.

head: Assume your
inputs will lie
body: Good systems do not need perfect inputs. Nobody gets perfect inputs.
They plan for the day the inputs lie.
